chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 477: The Doctor — Rehabilitation Becomes a Trap
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang enjoys lunch with his mother—until doctors arrive for 'rehabilitation.' In the Dao-Twisted World, Bai Lingmiao's sight fails and her spirit breaks. Two worlds, one trap.
og_title: The Doctor Arrives to 'Help' — And That's the Worst News of All
og_description: Li Huowang's quiet lunch with his mother shatters when doctors wheel in a chair. On the other side, Bai Lingmiao is going blind. Sometimes the worst threat is a kind voice.
twitter_title: Two worlds, one wheelchair. Li Huowang is about to lose everything to a doctor's good intentions.
twitter_description: Bai Lingmiao’s sight is fading. Li Huowang’s body is atrophying. And the doctors are coming to “help.” Ch. 477 of Dao Gui Yi Xian.

lore_anchors.definition: A traditional Chinese fire-starting tool made of steel struck against flint to create sparks, used for kindling campfires in rural or historical settings.
The iconic garment of Li Huowang in the Dao-Twisted World, stained red from violence and ritual. A visual marker of his identity and his descent.
A clinical term for physical therapy; in this chapter, it is repurposed as a method of forced separation from the parallel world, making medical care a psychological weapon.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can't Li Huowang leave the room?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His body in the Dao-Twisted World is currently walking into the woods alone. If his modern body is moved while he is lucid, he will lose his anchor and his other self may wander into danger or death.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Bai Lingmiao really going blind?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes. Her sight is slowly deteriorating, likely due to the corruption or spiritual strain of the Dao-Twisted World. She can still perceive blurry shapes and colors but can no longer see clearly.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Bai Lingmiao think they should separate?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She feels she is becoming a useless burden, and she suspects Li Huowang is lying to her about his recovery. Her love is mixed with guilt and the fear that they are dragging each other down.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the doctor good or evil?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Neither. The doctor is clinically well-intentioned, which makes him more terrifying. He has no idea that his "rehabilitation" will sever Li Huowang's connection to another world.
